newsitem.title: USA: USDA COTTON ESTIMATES NEUTRAL FOR PRICES-ANALYSTS.
newsitem.headline: USDA COTTON ESTIMATES NEUTRAL FOR PRICES-ANALYSTS.

text.p: The U.S. Department of Agriculture's 17.8 million bale estimate of the 1997/98 crop is not expected to nudge the market out of its recent trading range, industry analysts said.
They had pegged the USDA's August output estimate between 17.47 million and 18.15 million (480-lb) bales, compared to the July estimate of 18.00 million bales.
"The report overall is quite neutral," Ernest Simon, vice president with Prudential Securities, said.
The USDA left exports unchanged at 7.10 million bales and lowered ending stocks to 3.80 million bales versus last month's estimate of 3.95 million bales.
Sharon Johnson, an analyst with Frank Schneider and Co Inc, said the report could boost prices slightly since the market had anticipated a higher U.S. output estimate.
"I would say the report is neutral to slightly friendly from the standpoint that we have been down a lot recently and have priced in bearish report."
The December contract will need to close above 74.00 cents and then 75.20 cents in order to move higher, she said.
But Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes said higher estimates for production in India and Uzbekistan, and higher world ending stocks could offset any bullish effects of the domestic estimates.
Some analysts added that hot temperatures and good moisture levels across the cotton belt have helped to speed the development of U.S. cotton, and expect future estimates to reflect a larger crop.
